stem.en: Pteridophytes and bryophytes both lack flowers and seeds, yet they are placed in different groups. Which difference separates them?

text.en: Mosses have true roots, while ferns have only rhizoids.

feedback.en: This is the wrong way round: rhizoids belong to bryophytes, and true roots to ferns.

text.en: Ferns need water to reproduce, while mosses do not.

feedback.en: Both need water to reproduce, so this does not separate them.

text.en: Mosses grow in ponds, while ferns grow only in dry places.

feedback.en: Both grow in damp places, and habitat does not separate these two groups.

text.en: Ferns have true roots and vascular tissue; mosses do not.

feedback.en: Yes. True roots, stems and leaves, with xylem and phloem, make a plant a pteridophyte.

explanation.en: Bryophytes have rhizoids, simple leaf-like parts and no vascular tissue. Pteridophytes have true roots, stems and leaves, and they have xylem and phloem. Both still depend on water to reproduce.

hints.en: Look at the body and at what is inside the stem.
